'''''Opuntia tuna''''', known as '''sour pickle''', '''pricklypear''', or '''elephantear pricklypear''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Opuntia tuna |url=https://www.gbif.org/taxon/9Y783 |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=www.gbif.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=GSRS: Opuntia tuna fruit |url=https://precision.fda.gov/ginas/app/ui/substances/33cc8535-2e16-4daa-bb43-911b9e51de3c |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=precision.fda.gov}}</ref> is a species of [[cactus]] in the genus ''[[Opuntia]]''. 

== Distribution and habitat ==
Some sources say ''Opuntia tuna'' is endemic only to [[Jamaica]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Guiggi |first=Alessandro |last2=Mariotti |first2=Mauro |date=2022-11-23 |title=Taxonomic and nomenclatural novelties in some Cactaceae of Greater Antilles |url=https://phytotaxa.mapress.com/pt/article/view/phytotaxa.573.2.3 |journal=Phytotaxa |language=en |volume=573 |issue=2 |pages=215–230 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.573.2.3 |issn=1179-3163}}</ref> Some say the species is endemic to [[Hispaniola]], Jamaica, and other [[Caribbean]] islands.{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}} Some sources place the native range from Mexico to Jamaica, including Central America.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Opuntia tuna (L.) Mill. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:137125-1 |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> 

The species has been introduced in the [[southern United States]], the greater [[Caribbean]], northern [[Northern South America|South America]], [[Western Europe]], [[North Africa|Northern Africa]], [[Madagascar]], the [[Middle East]], [[South Asia|South]] and [[Southeast Asia]], and eastern [[Australia]].<ref name=":1" />
[[File:Opuntia10 filtered.jpg|thumb|Illustration of ''Opuntia jamaicensis'' (''O. tuna'') from ''The Cactaceae'' (1919-1923) by Britton et Rose, Vol. I, Plate XIX.]]

== Taxonomy ==
The first description was in 1753 by [[Carl Linnaeus]] as ''Cactus tuna''. [[Philip Miller]] described it as ''Opuntia tuna'' in 1768. In the early 19th century, it was renamed ''O. humbles'', ''O. polyanthus'', and ''O. dillenii''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Britton |first=N. L. |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Cactaceae/ru4sAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22Opuntia+tuna%22&pg=PA114&printsec=frontcover |title=The Cactaceae: Descriptions and Illustrations of Plants of the Cactus Family |date=1919 |publisher=Carnegie Institution of Washington |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Köhler |first=Matias |last2=Majure |first2=Lucas C. |last3=Franck |first3=Alan R. |last4=Campbell |first4=Keron C. St. E. |date=2025 |title=(3089) Proposal to reject the name Cactus tuna (Opuntia tuna) (Cactaceae) |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/tax.13365 |journal=TAXON |language=en |volume=74 |issue=3 |pages=734–735 |doi=10.1002/tax.13365 |issn=1996-8175}}</ref> 

In 2004, a paper in the journal ''Bradleya'' claimed that the taxon is a mix between ''O. tuna sensu'' (described by Britton & Rose in 1919) and ''O. dillenii.''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Crook |first=Richard |last2=Mottram |first2=Ray |date=May 2004 |title=Opuntia Index Part 10: T-V |url=https://bioone.org/journals/bradleya/volume-22/issue-22/brad.n22.2004.a7/Opuntia-Index-Part-10-T-V/10.25223/brad.n22.2004.a7.short |journal=Bradleya |volume=22 |issue=22 |pages=53-76}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2025, there was a proposal in [[Taxon (journal)|''Taxon'']] to reject the name ''Opuntia tuna'', with the authors arguing that what is being called ''O. tuna'' are actually multiple species (one endemic to Jamaica, which they argue should be called ''O. kingstoniana;'' and another which should be called ''O. dillenii'').<ref name=":2" />
